weeks.context: You're building beanforge.cafe — a 1-page website for a fictional specialty coffee shop named Bean Forge. We give you the menu, prices, hours, address, photos. Your job: ship it as a live HTML+CSS site on Netlify by Sunday. Why fictional? Because you finish in 1 week, not 6 — no waiting for a real owner to email back specs. Weeks 5-12 turn into a real SaaS clone. By Week 24 you have 4 named, live projects.

days.title: How the web works — 8-minute mental model
days.summary: Browser ↔ DNS ↔ server. Get the picture before the syntax.

items.title: Bean Forge spec — copy into your repo
items.why: If this URL 404s, just use the spec below: Name: Bean Forge. Tagline: 'Coffee, sharpened.' Menu: Espresso $3, Cortado $4, Pour Over $5, Cold Brew $5, Croissant $4. Hours: Mon-Fri 7am-6pm, Sat-Sun 8am-4pm. Address: 42 Anvil Street. Phone: +1 555-0142. Use Unsplash for photos.

days.title: HTML — the structure (semantic, not div soup)
days.summary: Real tags: header, main, section, footer. Not 50 divs.

items.title: HTML crash course — Web Dev Simplified
items.creator: Web Dev Simplified

items.title: Build the skeleton
items.body:
Create folder `beanforge/`. Create `index.html`. Build these sections with semantic tags (NO css yet):
  - `<header>` with nav links (Menu, Hours, Visit)
  - `<section id='hero'>` with the name + tagline + a Visit button
  - `<section id='menu'>` with the 5 menu items + prices as a `<ul>`
  - `<section id='hours'>` with the hours table (use `<table>`)
  - `<section id='visit'>` with address + phone + a map link
  - `<footer>` with © Bean Forge 2026
View in browser — should render readable text with no styling. Push to GitHub as repo `beanforge`.

days.title: CSS — the look (no framework)
days.summary: Modern CSS is good. Custom properties + flexbox cover 90%.

items.title: Style Bean Forge
items.body:
Create `style.css`. Required:
  - Custom properties at :root: `--coffee: #3b2418; --cream: #f5ead7;     --copper: #b87333;`
  - System font stack (no Google Fonts yet)
  - Hero: full-viewport, centered text, cream background, espresso photo as     a CSS background-image with overlay
  - Menu: 2-column grid on desktop, 1-column on mobile
  - Hours table: striped rows, centered
  - Buttons: copper background, cream text, hover lifts 2px
Use real Unsplash coffee photos (https://unsplash.com/s/photos/coffee — pick any). Inspect each image's hosted URL and hotlink (Unsplash allows this for free).

days.title: Responsive — mobile FIRST
days.summary: 70% of traffic is on phones. Don't make it an afterthought.

items.title: Test at 3 widths
items.body:
Add media queries:
  - Base styles (≤ 600px): single column, full-width buttons
  - `@media (min-width: 600px)`: 2-column menu, max-width: 1100px on main
  - `@media (min-width: 1024px)`: hero with 2-column (text + image)
Open Chrome DevTools → toggle device mode. Test at iPhone 13 (390px), iPad (768px), Desktop (1280px). Each should look intentional, not broken.

days.title: Click-to-call + Maps + favicon
days.summary: Real customers tap, they don't type.

items.title: Make Bean Forge contactable
items.body: In the Visit section: - Phone is a clickable `+1 555-0142` - Email `hello@beanforge.cafe` - 'Get Directions' button opens Google Maps: `Get Directions` Add a favicon: a coffee bean emoji as a 32×32 PNG. Use favicon.io to generate from text. Drop it in the repo root, link in ``.

days.title: Git + GitHub + Netlify deploy
days.summary: If it's not live, it doesn't exist.

items.title: Deploy static site to Netlify in 5 min
items.creator: various

items.title: Go live
items.body: Push the latest to GitHub. Go to netlify.com → New site from Git → connect GitHub → pick `beanforge` repo → Deploy. You get a *.netlify.app URL. Custom subdomain: in Netlify site settings → Domain → change to `yourname-beanforge.netlify.app`. Open the live URL on your phone. Tap the phone link — it should open the dialer.

days.title: Performance + SEO + ship
days.summary: Lighthouse ≥ 90 on Performance. That's the job.

items.title: Final polish — pass criteria
items.body:
□ Add meta description and Open Graph tags to `<head>`:
    <meta name='description' content='Bean Forge — specialty coffee, sharpened.'>
    <meta property='og:title' content='Bean Forge'>
    <meta property='og:image' content='[hero photo URL]'>
□ All images have `loading='lazy'` and width/height attrs (prevents layout shift)
□ Run Chrome DevTools → Lighthouse → Mobile → Performance ≥ 90, Accessibility ≥ 90,
    Best Practices ≥ 90, SEO ≥ 90. Screenshot the score.
□ README has: live URL at the top, Lighthouse screenshot, screenshot of the site
    on a phone, your name, 'Built for Bean Forge — Week 1 of FORGE Full-Stack Web'
□ Tag git release v0.1
□ Paste the live URL into a WhatsApp message to yourself — verify the OG preview
    shows the coffee photo + 'Bean Forge'

items.title: The 4-week arc
items.body: Week 2: JavaScript fundamentals + add an interactive menu filter. Week 3: add a contact form (Netlify Forms). Week 4: refactor into Astro for components + a /blog page. Project 1 ships at end of W4. Then Project 2 (W5-12) is a Next.js + Stripe SaaS.

weeks.title: JavaScript and TypeScript — The Language of the Web
weeks.context: JavaScript is the language. TypeScript is the language with the safety net. This week you become fluent in modern JS (ES2024+) and then add the type layer that turns chaos into code that scales.
topics: Modern JavaScript — const/let, destructuring, spread, optional chaining, nullish coalescing
Functions — arrow vs regular, this binding, closures
Asynchrony — Promises, async/await, why callback hell is dead
Modules — import/export, dynamic imports, why CommonJS is legacy
Iterables and generators — for...of, yield, async generators
TypeScript fundamentals — primitives, unions, intersections, type vs interface
Generics — when they help, when they hurt
Utility types — Partial, Pick, Omit, Record, ReturnType
tasks: Install Node.js 22+ (LTS) and pnpm (or use bun); set up a TypeScript project from scratch with tsconfig.json
Convert a 200-line JavaScript file (your or a tutorial's) to fully-typed TypeScript with no `any`
Build a fetch wrapper with typed responses using generics — `api<User>('/users/1')` returns Promise<User>
Solve 20 problems on JavaScript-only sites (HackerRank, Codewars, LeetCode easy) using modern syntax — no var, no callbacks
Write a generator function that yields Fibonacci numbers lazily; consume it with take(10)
weeks.project: Build a CLI Tool in TypeScript. Pick a real personal need — a markdown linter for your blog posts, a duplicate-file finder, a 'time spent in folders' tracker. Use commander.js for arg parsing, zod for input validation, strict TypeScript throughout. Publish to npm or install via `npx`. The CLI should be useful enough that you actually use it weekly.

weeks.title: Git, GitHub, and the Daily Development Loop
weeks.context: Git is more important than your framework. By Friday you can branch, merge, rebase, resolve conflicts, write good commit messages, open clean pull requests, and review someone else's PR thoughtfully — the daily work of every software engineer.
topics: Git mental model — commits as snapshots, branches as pointers, HEAD as a pointer to a pointer
The daily commands — clone, status, add, commit, push, pull, branch, checkout, merge, rebase
Conflict resolution — what a conflict actually is, how to read the markers, how to abort
Rewriting history — interactive rebase, squash, fixup, amend, when each is safe
Remotes — origin vs upstream, fetch vs pull, force-with-lease
Git workflows — trunk-based, GitFlow, GitHub Flow — what real teams use
Good commit messages — Conventional Commits, the imperative form, why it matters
Pull requests — small, atomic, reviewable; how to write a description

On one of your earlier projects, write commit messages that follow Conventional Commits (feat:, fix:, chore:); rewrite history with interactive rebase to clean up

Find an open-source project; fork it, fix a typo or improve a docstring, open a real PR upstream
Practice the rebase-on-stale-main workflow: rebase your feature branch onto an updated main, resolve any conflicts cleanly
weeks.project: Make a Real Open-Source Contribution. Pick a project you use (one of your dependencies — Next.js, FastAPI, requests, axios). Find a 'good first issue' or a typo in docs. Read CONTRIBUTING.md. Fork, branch, fix, commit conventionally, open a PR with a clear description. Engage with feedback. Get the PR merged (or closed with a clear reason). Lists and keys — why keys matter for reconciliation
Rendering performance — memo, useMemo, useCallback, when each is worth it (often: not)
